newsitem.title: UK: BA up on hopes of go-ahead for Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: BA up on hopes of go-ahead for Eurofighter.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc gained on Wednesday amid hopes that Germany would give the green light for the four-country Eurofighter project, analysts and dealers said.
By 0845 GMT British Aerospace was up 8p to 12.25-1/2 stg.
"This would be good news for British Aerospace", a trader said. "The markets believe in the project as one can see today," he said.
Earlier, a senior German opposition politician said in an interview with BBC Radio that he had been assured that the government would come up with acceptable proposals for funding the project.
The development of the Eurofighter has been hampered in the past years by political struggles in Germany over how the new fighter should be funded.

Wednesday's meeting between British Defence Secretary George Robertson and his counterpart Volker Ruehe in Germany could also pave the way for Eurofighter approval which is seen as crucial for thousands of British jobs.
William Mackie, analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said he expected the share to rise in the next six to eight months but said 13.50 stg was the "upper side".
Apart from Eurofighter, the recent termination of Jetstream aircraft production in Scotland was favourable for British Aerospace, he said.
